question: Solve $\dfrac{1}{x} < 2$.
trap: x could be negative. Never multiply by x.

beats.say: Most students get this wrong. Solve one over X is less than two.
Many multiply both sides by X. One is less than two X, so X is greater than a half.
But X could be negative, and multiplying by a negative flips the sign. Never multiply by X. Bring everything to one side, as one fraction.
The top is zero at a half. The bottom is zero at zero. Test the signs on a number line.
The fraction is negative when X is less than zero, or X is greater than a half.
Check with X equals negative one. One over negative one is negative one, which is less than two. The shortcut missed it.
More like this, free, at adrian math tuition dot com.

verify:
x = symbols('x', real=True)
sol = solve_univariate_inequality(1/x < 2, x, relational=False)
assert sol == Union(Interval.open(-oo, 0), Interval.open(Rational(1, 2), oo))
assert simplify(1/x - 2 - (1 - 2*x)/x) == 0
# signs on the number line: -, +, -
f = (1 - 2*x)/x
assert f.subs(x, -1) < 0 and f.subs(x, Rational(1, 4)) > 0 and f.subs(x, 1) < 0
assert (1/x).subs(x, -1) < 2      # the root the shortcut loses

youtube.title: Solve 1/x < 2 (multiplying by x loses half the answer)
youtube.description: Solve 1/x < 2. Multiplying by x gives x > ½ — but x could be negative. Bring everything to one side: (1 − 2x)/x < 0, so x < 0 or x > ½.
